  -c "SELECT count(*) AS true_customer_count FROM customers;"
match: docker compose -f labs/sql/_stack/compose.yaml exec -T -e PGPASSWORD=demo-password postgres psql -U support -d support_lab -A --pset=footer=off -c "SELECT count(*) AS true_customer_count FROM customers;"

entries.command:
docker compose -f labs/sql/_stack/compose.yaml exec -T \
  -e PGPASSWORD=demo-password postgres \
  psql -U support -d support_lab -A -F'|' --pset=footer=off \
  -c "SELECT c.id, c.name, c.plan FROM customers c LEFT JOIN workspaces w ON w.customer_id = c.id WHERE w.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.id;"
match: docker compose -f labs/sql/_stack/compose.yaml exec -T -e PGPASSWORD=demo-password postgres psql -U support -d support_lab -A -F'|' --pset=footer=off -c "SELECT c.id, c.name, c.plan FROM customers c LEFT JOIN workspaces w ON w.customer_id = c.id WHERE w.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.id;"

entries.command:

entries.output:
-- Plan mix report: how many customers are on each plan.
-- Edit this until it answers the question correctly, then run `tse check`.
SELECT c.plan, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM customers c
JOIN workspaces w ON w.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.plan
ORDER BY c.plan;
